notation.title: Juxtaposition means multiplication
notation.text: Anything written next to anything else, with no symbol between, means multiply: 3x, 2(x+1), (a+1)(a-1), xy are all products.

notation.title: The minus sign is one of three things
notation.text: Binary subtraction (a - b), unary negation (-a), or multiply-by-(-1) in front of a bracket -(...). When a minus confuses you, ask which of the three it is.

notation.title: Brackets carry an implicit operation in front
notation.text: No explicit symbol before a bracket means multiplication (M1). A minus before a bracket means times (-1) (M2).

notation.title: Exponents bind tighter than coefficients and signs
notation.text: -a^2 means -(a^2), not (-a)^2. The exponent applies first, the minus after.

notation.title: The fraction bar is a bracket
notation.text: Everything above the line is one grouped object, everything below another. a + b/c and (a+b)/c are different things.

structure.title: The dominant operation is the last one applied
structure.text: If you evaluated the expression step by step, the operation you would do last is the dominant one. Everything else happens inside chunks.

structure.title: Brackets make a chunk
structure.text: Whatever is inside brackets is a single object. The dominant operation is always outside all brackets.

structure.title: Multiplication binds tighter than addition and subtraction
structure.text: In 3x + 2y the multiplication is used up inside the terms; the dominant operation is the +. It is a sum, not a product.

structure.title: The dominant operation determines which tools apply
structure.text: Sum or difference: collect like terms, look for common factors. Product: expand or factor. Power: power rules. Quotient: fraction manipulation.
